answers.U1-S1: Seeing flamingos as a six-year-old was the greatest experience of the narrator's life, and nothing he ever saw afterward could compare to it.
answers.U1-S2: He was a fearful, timid boy who was scared of animals and of the outdoors in general, and wasn't brave enough to go anywhere alone.
answers.U1-S3: To show the walk was long, hard and exhausting for a small boy, so the plain was a difficult, almost dangerous place for children.
answers.U1-S4: Seriously and slowly, in a grave, dignified way.
answers.U1-S5: Because the open wings showed a glorious crimson color he hadn't expected, making the bird look like an angel.
answers.U1-S6: That flamingos were extremely rare, a bird almost nobody in the whole region had ever seen, so the boys had witnessed something truly unusual.
answers.U1-S7: Because its beauty, white-and-rose body and crimson wings seemed heavenly and perfect to him, more beautiful than anything else in the world.
answers.U1-S8: Because nothing can ever match the first time you see something; as you grow up you lose the ability to feel real wonder.
answers.U1-S9: It shows that the first sighting was the best moment of his life, proving childhood experiences are always more powerful than anything adults feel.
answers.U1-S10: Deeply nostalgic and longing; he treasures the memory and feels his adult life has never been as wonderful.
